content:
anya: quick heads-up — ran a 24h long-context chat load on Private and Dedicated and saw steady kv cache growth on Private (no OOM yet but linear mem increase). looks like background compaction isn't happening.

matt: can you paste top-level numbers? is this across multiple GPUs or a single node?

anya: single onprem box (A100 80GB), Dedicated run on gcp n1-standard + nvlink cluster for contrast. Private host shows +8GB over 24h for similar qps. Dedicated flat after warmup.

lina: perf-bot attached sampling summary: total_kv_pages_alloc=1.2M vs 950k, evict_count lower on Private, page_frag_ratio higher.

perf-bot: sampling snapshot 
```
host: private-onprem-03
kv_alloc_pages: 1245120
kv_evicted_pages: 3120
kv_compaction_runs: 1
page_fragmentation_ratio: 0.37
```

sam: hmm compaction_runs=1 over 24h is wrong. background thread probably paused by jemalloc configuration or blocked by IO when compaction tries to sweep. On our Hosted infra compaction thread runs frequently.

rahul: cc @lina — do we have different MALLOC_CONF or hugepage settings in the Private image? VPC images historically set MADV_NOHUGEPAGE and tune for latency.

lina: checked — Private base image sets MALLOC_CONF=lg_dirty_mult:8,background_thread:0 for historical stability. Dedicated and Hosted set background_thread:1.

matt: that explains it. background_thread:0 will prevent async page recycling, forcing compaction into allocation paths which is expensive and may get skipped under sustained load.

anya: curious why we set background_thread:0 for Private originally — IIRC to avoid noisy threads under constrained management. but for long-context KV reuse we need steady compaction.

sam: also noticed batching heuristics interact. Private deployment has smaller default max_batch latency (to meet SLOs), which keeps many frames resident longer and delays eviction. combined with no background compaction -> fragmentation.

lina: reproducer I ran locally: start model w/ --kv-pages=200k, run steady tail queries with long prefix reuse. on Private config: mem rises. switching MALLOC_CONF to background_thread:1 fixed steady-state within 15 minutes.

anya: paste of the quick repro commands:
```
# run load generator
./tools/loadgen --qps 50 --ctx 4096 --prefix-cache=on --duration 2h --target private:5001
# mem snapshots every 5m
for i in {1..24}; do pmap $(pgrep runtime) | tail -n1; sleep 300; done
```

rahul: caution — on some VPCs we disabled background threads because of noisy neighbor CPU scheduling and throttling on k8s node pools. If we enable it by default on Private, we should gate with feature flag or make it tunable per-cluster.

matt: agree. propose: make background_thread default to 1 in runtime images unless cluster annotates "low-cpu-noisy". Also add an autoset that flips with node label.

lina: also want to add a compaction health metric to console: compaction_runs_per_min and page_frag_ratio. right now we only surface raw memory and evictions.

sam: small kernel-level note: onprem nodes with 2-socket NUMA and hugepage fragmentation showed slower fallback to small pages which increases vm fragmentation. we should add a NUMA-aware compaction path and tune THP.

anya: action items:
- matt: add MALLOC_CONF auto flag + cluster annotation gating (PR)
- lina: add compaction metrics to console + alert if frag_ratio>0.25 for 30m
- sam: write short NUMA guidance doc and test THP vs no-THP on our onprem fleet
- rahul: coordinate patch rollout to Private images and validate on canary cluster

matt: I'll open the PR today, tag @anya for review.

lina: created a dashboard draft and will share link in #eng-runtime once done.

deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled for private-canary-02 at 03:00 UTC with MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:1

anya: thanks all, this felt like an obscure interaction between kernel/allocator/batching but easy win. will follow up with perf numbers after canary. :thumbsup:
